correction: STORY-01-007 wired the otel-collector service in docker-compose.yml with a bind-mount to _infra/docker/observability/otel-config.yaml, but never wrote the config file itself. On first `compose up`, Docker silently created an empty DIRECTORY at the bind-mount path, and the collector crashed with `read /etc/otel/config.yaml: is a directory`.
pattern: Whenever a generated docker-compose service declares a bind-mount to a host file (volumes: ./path/to/file.ext:/container/path), that host file MUST be authored in the same skill run. Bind-mounts to non-existent host paths cause Docker to auto-create an empty directory, which then masquerades as a 'file' to the container and produces confusing 'is a directory' errors. Before finishing, the skill must enumerate every `volumes:` entry whose source is a file path (has an extension) and assert the source file exists on disk with non-empty content.

correction: STORY-01-010's reconciliation integration test was emitted at tests/utils/test_reconciliation_integration.py. It boots a real SparkSession (via pyspark.importorskip + delta), so a stale Py4J/PySpark venv produces _start_update_server() arity errors that turn the unit-test job red even though no unit code is broken. Worse, STORY-01-002 AC5 runs bare `pytest tests/utils/` which picks up this integration test by path and fails-closed. The unit/integration split has to be enforced by layout, not just by marker.
pattern: Integration tests (any test that imports pyspark, boots a SparkSession, requires Docker, or talks to UC OSS / Marquez) MUST be emitted under tests/integration/<layer>/, NEVER under tests/<layer>/ alongside unit tests. The marker @pytest.mark.integration is required but not sufficient — the path itself encodes the contract so that `pytest tests/<layer>/` is unambiguously unit-only. Additionally: when the scaffold writes a Makefile, `make test` MUST be `uv run pytest -m "not integration" tests/` (or equivalently `uv run pytest tests/<layer>/ tests/<layer>/ ...` excluding tests/integration), and a separate `make integration-test` target MUST run `uv run pytest -m integration tests/integration/`. Story ACs that assert `pytest tests/utils/` green should be regenerated to assert `make test` green so the AC tracks the Make-target contract, not a path that may include integration tests.

correction: STORY-01-007's Dockerfile.airflow used `FROM python:3.12-slim` (rolling tag). When Debian 13/trixie became the default slim base, the build started failing with `apt-get install openjdk-17-jdk-headless` exit 100 because trixie dropped openjdk-17 in favor of openjdk-21. Previous successful builds were either before the tag rolled or relied on a stale local layer cache, masking the regression until a fresh build.
pattern: Always pin Debian releases explicitly in container base images. NEVER use floating tags like `python:3.12-slim`, `debian:slim`, `ubuntu:latest`, or any tag that omits the distro release codename. Use the release-pinned form: `python:3.12-slim-bookworm`, `debian:12-slim`, `ubuntu:24.04`. When the LLD pins a system package (JDK version, Spark version, glibc), the Dockerfile MUST pin the base distro release that ships that package — verify the package exists in the chosen release before emitting the FROM line. This eliminates the entire class of bug where the same Dockerfile builds today, breaks tomorrow when the upstream rolling tag rotates, and the local layer cache hides the regression until a clean rebuild.

correction: STORY-01-007 Dockerfile.airflow fetched Spark from `https://dlcdn.apache.org/spark/spark-4.0.0/spark-4.0.0-bin-hadoop3-scala2.13.tgz`. The URL had two bugs: (a) `dlcdn.apache.org` is a rolling mirror that only serves the CURRENT release line — once Spark 4.0.0 was superseded (by 4.0.2 / 4.1.1) the dlcdn path returned 404; (b) starting with Spark 4.x, Scala 2.13 is the default and the binary name has NO `-scala2.13` suffix — the correct artifact is `spark-4.0.0-bin-hadoop3.tgz`. The mv target path was also wrong for the same reason.
pattern: When fetching pinned versions of Apache project releases (Spark, Kafka, Flink, Hadoop, etc.) in a Dockerfile or installer, NEVER use `https://dlcdn.apache.org/` — that mirror only carries the currently-supported releases, so pins to older versions silently start 404-ing the moment Apache rotates them. ALWAYS use `https://archive.apache.org/dist/` for version-pinned downloads, which preserves every historical release. Additionally, verify the exact artifact name for the target version against the archive directory listing before emitting the URL — naming conventions change across major versions (e.g. Spark 3.x ships `-bin-hadoop3-scala2.13.tgz`, but Spark 4.x drops the `-scala2.13` suffix because Scala 2.13 is the only build). The skill MUST `curl -sI` the resolved URL during generation and fail loudly if it 404s, rather than emitting an untested URL.

correction: The create-scaffold skill emitted a custom `Dockerfile.airflow` (FROM python:3.12-slim, download Spark binary from dlcdn) that diverged from the canonical cookiecutter template (FROM apache/airflow:3.2.1-python3.11, install pyspark via pip with no Spark binary download). The custom file shipped both L-002 and L-003 bugs; the template did not. The divergence was invisible until the build actually ran, because nothing in the skill or downstream validators compares rendered output against the template.
pattern: Always render scaffold files BY APPLYING the cookiecutter template, NEVER by re-deriving them from the LLD inline. Specifically: any file that has a corresponding source under `inputs/lld/v*/templates/cookiecutter-chapter/{{cookiecutter.chapter_name}}/{{cookiecutter.project_name}}/...` MUST be produced by cookiecutter variable substitution on that source — not by the skill authoring a parallel implementation. After every create-scaffold run the skill MUST diff every rendered file against the template source (post variable substitution) and FAIL LOUDLY if any path under the template exists in patient_360/ with materially different content. This catches the silent-divergence class of bug where the LLD describes a service one way, the template encodes a tested way, and the skill emits a third untested way.

correction: patient_360/_infra/docker/docker-compose.yml mapped Marquez API to host port 5000 (`5000:5000`), colliding with macOS AirPlay Receiver which binds 0.0.0.0:5000 by default on macOS 12+. The cookiecutter template (`inputs/.../docker-compose.yml`) already maps host 5001 -> container 5000 specifically to dodge this collision, but the scaffold skill rendered a divergent file with the wrong mapping (same class as L-004). Result: `make dev-up` failed with `bind: address already in use` on a stock macOS dev machine.
pattern: When emitting host-port mappings in a Dockerfile / docker-compose for a project that may be developed on macOS, NEVER bind host ports 5000 or 7000 — Apple's AirPlay Receiver and AirTunes claim those ports by default on macOS 12+ and the user cannot change that without disabling AirPlay system-wide. Pick a non-reserved host port (5001+, 7001+) and document the mapping in a comment. Prefer parameterized form via env-var with a safe default: `"${SERVICE_HOST_PORT:-5001}:5000"` so developers can override without editing the compose file. This rule applies to ANY service whose canonical default port is 5000 or 7000 (Marquez API, Flask default, Python http.server default). Additionally — see L-004 — the rendered compose file MUST match the template; the skill should diff every rendered _infra/docker/* path against `inputs/lld/v*/templates/.../...` and fail loudly on divergence.

correction: patient_360 docker-compose.yml + the cookiecutter template both set the Airflow service healthcheck to `curl http://localhost:8080/health`. Airflow 3.x moved that endpoint to `/api/v2/monitor/health`; the legacy `/health` returns 404. Result: every Airflow container Docker brings up is marked `unhealthy` forever, Airflow itself runs fine, but `docker compose up --wait` blocks until timeout and `make dev-up` exits with code 1. Confirmed in patient_360-airflow: /health => 404, /api/v2/monitor/health => 200.
pattern: When emitting a healthcheck for a vendor service (Airflow, Marquez, Unity Catalog, Postgres, etc.), pin the health URL to the version-specific path documented for the pinned image — and verify it returns 200 against that image BEFORE writing the compose. For Airflow specifically: 1.x/2.x served `/health`, 3.x serves `/api/v2/monitor/health` (the v1 API was removed and `/health` returns 404). Whenever the LLD pins an Airflow major version >=3, the healthcheck MUST use the v2 monitor endpoint. As a general rule, never copy a healthcheck URL from older docs without re-verifying against the pinned image — vendors routinely renumber API paths across majors, and Docker silently keeps the container in `unhealthy` state when the check 404s.

correction: patient_360 + cookiecutter template + LIBRARIES.md all pin `pyspark==4.0.0`. That release is broken: `pyspark/core/context.py:309` calls `_start_update_server(auth_token)` with one arg, but `pyspark/accumulators.py:357` requires `(auth_token, is_unix_domain_sock, socket_path=None)` — a two-arg minimum. Every SparkContext init in PySpark 4.0.0 raises `TypeError: _start_update_server() missing 1 required positional argument: 'is_unix_domain_sock'`. The bug blocks any code that imports pyspark and boots a SparkSession: unit tests, integration tests, and the runtime DAG. Upstream fixed it in 4.0.1 (line 309 now passes is_unix_domain_sock). The same bug was previously misdiagnosed in L-001 as 'Py4J version drift' and worked around by routing integration tests via marker — but the real defect is PySpark 4.0.0 itself.
pattern: NEVER pin `pyspark==4.0.0` — that exact version ships a regression in `pyspark/core/context.py` that breaks every SparkSession boot with a TypeError on `_start_update_server`. Pin `pyspark>=4.0.2,<4.1` (last patch in the 4.0 line, fully wire-compatible with a Spark 4.0.0 JVM) or upgrade to `pyspark==4.1.1` if the LLD's Spark JVM pin permits the 4.1 line. Before emitting any PySpark pin in a Dockerfile, pyproject.toml, or LIBRARIES.md, the skill MUST `pip install <pin>` in a throwaway venv and run `python -c 'from pyspark.sql import SparkSession; SparkSession.builder.master("local[1]").getOrCreate().stop()'` — if SparkContext init raises, the pin is rejected. The earlier 'pyspark/py4j version drift' workaround in L-001 (marker-based unit/integration split) does NOT fix this — it only hides the symptom in unit tests; integration runs, smoke-se, and the Bronze DAG still die. The honest fix is to bump the pin off 4.0.0.

correction: validate-ingestion check_soft_import_removed flags try/except ImportError around se_runner as CRITICAL once se_runner.py ships, but LLD §8.6 + §13 Decision 14 (Resolved 2026-05-11) explicitly require keeping it as a diagnostic-only fail-closed wrapper that re-raises. STORY-01-009 ships this pattern with a passing test.
pattern: When the validator finding contradicts the latest LLD revision, do NOT remove the diagnostic try/except ImportError wrapper from ingestion_runner.py — it is mandated by LLD §8.6 + §13 Decision 14. The validator rule check_soft_import_removed needs to be updated to recognize the diagnostic-only pattern (log + re-raise) as compliant, distinct from the legacy soft-import bootstrap (swallow + continue).

correction: Forked Skill invocations of create-dag/update-ingestion sometimes return without running Phase 0 resolver — `.skill-arg`/`.skill-paths` remain on disk and the skill claims no user request was given. create-ingestion appears more reliable.
pattern: When a forked skill returns asking for a target, the orchestrator should retry with the conversational arg explicitly OR detect that .skill-arg was not consumed (file still present after invocation) and surface a CRITICAL halt rather than silently moving on.

correction: STORY-02-005 AC1/AC3 specify dq_rules/synthea_*.yml but LLD §5.1 + project CLAUDE.md use dq_rules/{table}.yml convention
pattern: When story AC glob conflicts with LLD/project convention, halt and recommend scrum-master:update-stories rather than rename project-wide

correction: contracts/{table}.yml in STORY-02-001 AC is a reference (existing contract used by ingestion runner), not a scaffold deliverable; classifier grouped it under scaffold but the sub-skill correctly ROUTE-OUTed.

correction: STORY-02-005 AC2/AC3 verification spec uses equals:13 (row_dq) and equals:6 (action_if_failed) — counts file occurrences not files-with-rule. Real files have multiple rules per YAML per DQS spec; spec should use min:13 / min:6 with per-file constraint.
pattern: When AC Verification uses grep_count equals:N where N == file count, but each file legitimately contains multiple matches, the verification spec is wrong; flag to scrum-master for spec correction rather than reduce real rule content.
